study_identification_part.si_4_title: Analyzing heterogeneity in Alzheimer disease using multimodal normative modeling on imaging-based ATN biomarkers

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Multimodal variational autoencoder (mmVAE) used as the normative modeling framework.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: This framework is based on a multimodal variational autoencoder (mmVAE), which takes as input cross-sectional ATN biomarker data including regional gray matter volumes, as well as amyloid FBP and tau FTP SUVR values (Figure S1).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Kumar2025.pdf.md: 2.5 Multimodal normative modeling / 2.5.1 Model training

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Regional gray matter volumes and regional amyloid-FBP and tau-FTP SUVR values (66 cortical + 24 subcortical ROIs per modality) were modeled as ATN inputs.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: This framework is based on a multimodal variational autoencoder (mmVAE), which takes as input cross-sectional ATN biomarker data including regional gray matter volumes, as well as amyloid FBP and tau FTP SUVR values (Figure S1).
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Kumar2025.pdf.md: 2.5 Multimodal normative modeling / 2.5.1 Model training

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Model conditioned on age and sex to remove covariate effects.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: mmVAE was conditioned on the age and sex of participants to remove the effect of covariates (see Supplementary Methods SM4.3).
